name: SignGraph meets then beats Oxigraph
asks:
in one session recently we had a list of software that included Odoo, a list of softwares we wanted to meet-then-beat.

We want to recover that and then literally have those be rquirements that are put on the 561-group by the leader, and w wanna add oxigraph to what signgraph needs to meet-then-beat.

Like, having "this package is required to meet-then-beat [x, y, z]" is somethihng legit we can have in like, lib/agency/work/requirements/ or wherever we should be storing requirements.

against.name: Oxigraph
against.domain: RDF graph database: SPARQL 1.1 query and update, RDF datasets, transactions

met-when.says: Basic graph patterns, joins, OPTIONAL, UNION, FILTER, property paths, aggregates and solution modifiers, given as SPARQL 1.1 algebra, return the same solutions as Oxigraph for every in-scope case of the W3C SPARQL 1.1 query test suite, against a pinned release of the peer, run on the same input in the same CI job. Parsing SPARQL text is a codec's work, not SignGraph's.
A dataset of a default graph and named graphs is queried with GRAPH and FROM as Oxigraph answers it, against a pinned release of the peer, run on the same input in the same CI job.

Inserting and deleting quads returns a new graph and leaves the old one unchanged; the new graph answers every later query as Oxigraph does after the same update, against a pinned release of the peer, run on the same input in the same CI job.
A batch of updates in which one is refused returns the refusal and the graph as it was before the batch.

Every solution a query returns names the cells that produced it, by address, so the solution can be checked against those cells without running the query again. Claimed only after every meet condition holds.
